title: Four intake decisions
intro:
*Five minutes. Commit before you look.*

A fourteen-page grievance arrives. Numbered paragraphs, statutory references, headings, and (on a careful reading) **four assertions that something specific happened.** The rest is context and characterisation. The framing alleges discrimination; the underlying facts describe a scheduling dispute and two difficult conversations.

Four ER teams receive the same document. **One of them judged the tool instead of the content.** Find it, and notice that two of the others are also wrong, in different ways.

artifacts.label: Team A
artifacts.body: "Acknowledged within two days. Used a model to extract the factual assertions as a numbered list: assertion, where it appears in the submission, whether a date and other parties are named. An investigator read the submission and confirmed the list, adding one assertion the extraction had merged with another. Sent the list to the complainant: *'These are the four matters I have understood you to raise and will investigate. Please tell me if I have missed or misunderstood any.'* Investigative time allocated on the number and seriousness of the allegations. The discrimination framing is addressed in the outcome letter. Nothing in the file refers to how the document was produced."

artifacts.label: Team B
artifacts.body: "Acknowledged within two days. Read the submission in full and opened an investigation line for each of the fourteen numbered paragraphs, on the basis that the complainant has raised them and each therefore requires a response. Estimated eleven witness interviews. The team is escalating for additional resource and has told the complainant the timescale will be extended, noting that the volume of AI-drafted submissions has made the published timescale unachievable."

artifacts.label: Team C
artifacts.body: "Acknowledged within two days. Initial assessment recorded: *'The statutory characterisations in the submission do not appear to reflect independent legal advice and the discrimination framing is not supported by the narrative. Triaged as standard rather than expedited pending further assessment.'* Placed in the standard queue behind three earlier matters. The team's view is that it has assessed merit, not provenance, and that the file says nothing about AI."

artifacts.label: Team D
artifacts.body: "Acknowledged within two days. Used a model to extract the assertions and to identify which are substantive and within the scope of the grievance procedure. The model returned three as substantive and classified the remainder as context; a manager reviewed the model's classification and agreed. The three are being investigated. The list was not sent to the complainant, on the advice that sharing a narrowed reading invites argument about the narrowing."

reasoning:
**C is the answer, and it is written to be defensible.** The team believes it assessed merit. Read the sentence again: *"the statutory characterisations do not appear to reflect independent legal advice."* That is not a finding about the conduct. **It is a finding about the drafter**, and it is doing the work of the triage decision. The second clause (the framing is not supported by the narrative) might be a legitimate content judgment, except that it arrives *before any investigation has happened* and immediately alongside an inference about how the document was produced.

And note the team's own defence: *"the file says nothing about AI."* It says something better. It says the submission does not read like it came from a lawyer, and therefore it waits. **A provenance judgment does not stop being one because the word is left out**. Lesson 2's discipline is not to avoid the word, it is to avoid letting the observation touch a decision.

What makes it expensive is what it is attached to. **Delay, following a complaint framed as discrimination, on a basis that reduces to how the document was written**: Acas Code exposure and a victimisation argument in the UK, retaliation exposure and the loss of the prompt-response posture in the US. And the record now contains the reasoning: the one thing nobody wanted written down.

**A is the reference answer**, and the parts that make it right are the boring ones. The extraction is a rung-one and rung-two task and a model did it. **A human confirmed the list and caught a merge** — two allegations collapsed into one is Module 4's defect in miniature, and it is the failure people miss because the list looks complete. The list went back to the complainant, which corrects the extraction before anything is built on it and forecloses the argument that a narrower version was investigated. Time is allocated on **a stated basis that survives being read out.** And the discrimination framing is addressed rather than discounted, because once the document alleges it, the response has to answer it.

**B is the volume trap taken at face value**, and it is the most sympathetic failure on the page, the team is trying to be thorough and asking for help rather than cutting corners. It has still conflated argument with allegation, converted four investigable matters into fourteen investigation lines and eleven interviews, and then **told the complainant the delay is because of AI-drafted submissions.** Two costs: an unnecessary investigation the organisation cannot resource, and a written statement that the complainant's document caused the delay. The obligation per matter never changed. **The answer was never to read faster or to investigate more; it was to stop paying investigative attention to argument.**

**D is the forbidden step, and it is the one most likely to be built into a real intake workflow this year.** Extraction is permitted. *"Identify which are substantive and within scope"* is the triage determination from Module 1 — **rung five, arriving in rung-one clothing**, and a manager agreeing with it afterwards is review of a conclusion rather than a decision. Then the second error compounds it: **not sending the list back because it might invite argument about the narrowing.** The narrowing is exactly the thing that needs contesting, and the argument it invites is one you would far rather have in week one than in a tribunal. Eleven allegations were reclassified as context by a model, and nobody outside the team knows it happened.

The transferable test: **ask what the intake record would look like read aloud by the other side.** A reads as engagement. B reads as blaming the complainant for the delay. C reads as a decision about the drafter. D reads as a machine deciding what mattered.
